title: Exploring Chemistry and Confinement in Engineered 2D hBN using Aberration-Corrected STEM and Monochromated EELS
content: Many of the most exciting properties of 2D materials emerge not from a perfect lattice, but from controlled interruption of it. For example, atomic vacancies and dopants can be introduced to create functionalized nanopores [1] or quantum emitters [2], while moiré potential landscapes in twisted stacks can trap excitons to form quantum dot-like arrays [3]. Aberration-corrected scanning transmission electron microscopy (STEM) [4], combined with monochromated electron energy loss spectroscopy (EELS) and direct electron detection [5,6], is uniquely suited to exploring these effects, enabling atomic-scale mapping directly correlated with spectral signatures with an energy resolution down to a few meV.
